etymologies.etymologyHTML: First attested about 1380. From Middle English abundaunt, habundaunt, aboundant, from Anglo-Norman abundant, from Old French abondant, from Latin abundāns, present participle of abundo (“to overflow, to abound”). Compare abound.

definitions.definition: Fully sufficient; found in copious supply; in great quantity; overflowing. [First attested around 1350 to 1470.][3]

quote.citation: a. 1859, Leigh Hunt, On the Realities of Imagination:
quote.text: [W]ith their magical words they [poets] bring forth to our eyesight the abundant images and beauties of creation.

quote.citation: 2017, BioWare, Mass Effect: Andromeda (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →OCLC, PC, scene: Kadara:
quote.text: Kadara was of great interest to the Andromeda Initiative after it appeared on long-range surveys. Seemingly abundant liquid water and an oxygen-mix atmosphere made it a strong candidate for settlement, earning it the designation Habitat 4. Closer range surveys now reveal that Kadara's water sources are tainted and unpotable.

definitions.definition: Richly supplied; wealthy; possessing in great quantity. [First attested around 1350 to 1470.][3]

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Exodus 34:6:

definitions.definition: (mathematics) Being an abundant number, i.e. less than the sum of all of its divisors except itself. [First attested in the mid 16th century.][3]
